description: Ways to get items that are not crafting or furnace recipes (breaking blocks, using a tool on a block, the start kit), for howToGet. Hand-written from docs/research/rotn-progression.md, which cites the RotN wiki ([W-...]), the in-game handbook ([HB ...]) and the pinned pack's scripts and configs ([R:...]). Every rule names its evidence. confidence: 'documented' = a cited source states it; 'inferred' = derived from dumped names or a documented rule applied to variants the source does not name. 'unverified' lists the parts no harness run has checked yet. In rules with 'pairs' or 'stoneFamilies' the confidence is per pair: a pair is 'documented' only if it says "documented": true (or is in documentedMetas), otherwise 'inferred'. The dump's own block drops (getItemDropped with a fixed seed) miss event-handler drops such as Pyrotech's stone-to-rocks, so these rules come first.

sources.summary: Break a rock pile on the ground by hand; it drops the rock of its own type (the item meta equals the block meta). Near the G3 spawn most piles are Underground Biomes rock piles (pyrotech_compat:rock_metamorphic, _igneous, _sedimentary).
evidence: docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 1 step 1: [W-Getting_Started] 'rocks from rock piles on the ground'
G2 batch 5 (coord/STATUS-harness-ops.md): pyrotech:rock piles with metas 6 and 8 near spawn, so rock piles generate in the Overworld
the dump: pyrotech:rock block states 0-10 and item variants 0-10 have the same names (Stone Rock, ..., Red Sandstone Rock)

the dump (blocks.json): pyrotech_compat:rock_igneous (metas 0-7), rock_metamorphic (0-7) and rock_sedimentary (0-5), classes trinsdar.pyrotech_compat.block.rocks.BlockRock*: every state has no collision box, hardness 0.1 and no harvest tool, and drops the item of the same name and the same meta (getItemDropped/damageDropped); each state's variant matches the item variant's display name (rock_red_granite / Red Granite Rock, rock_soapstone / Soapstone Rock, rock_chalk / Chalk Rock, ...). These items are in the 'rock' ore dictionary (wildcard meta), so they make the crude axe, Crafting Tools and stone tools

S1-A survey (coord/STATUS-harness-ops.md; test/evidence/s1/s1a-20261102/survey/result.json), G2 world, radius 48 around the fresh spawn: pyrotech_compat:rock_metamorphic meta 0 (81 blocks) and 6 (23), rock_igneous 0 (71) and 7 (8), rock_sedimentary 0 (15), 1 (1) and 2 (1); pyrotech:rock only meta 4 (3, a Dirt Clump)

which piles give a rock that rock recipes accept: the dump's oredict.json 'rock' (packages/rotn-data/3.3.4/oredict.json): pyrotech:rock metas 0, 6 and 8 only; pyrotech_compat:rock_igneous, rock_metamorphic and rock_sedimentary every meta (wildcard 32767). The crude axe, Crafting Tools and the stone pickaxe and axe take ore 'rock' (or flint). howToGet lists, per rule block, the metas whose drop is in the ore ('ore' on the way)
sources.inferred: The Underground Biomes rock piles (no documented flag): the research names rock piles in general and pyrotech:rock; the Underground Biomes piles and their drops come from the dump only.
unverified: that breaking a pile by hand gives exactly one item of the same meta in game (the dump's drop is getItemDropped, without event handlers)
sources.note: Metas 4 (Dirt Clump), 5 (Sand Pile), 7 (Pile of Wood Chips) and 9 (Red Sand Pile) of pyrotech:rock are not rocks: they are not in the 'rock' ore dictionary, so they do not work in rock recipes. pyrotech:rock_grass (149 blocks in S1-A) drops a Grass Clump, also not a rock.

sources.summary: Break a Dynamic Trees branch, by hand or with an axe (no tool is required; use an axe when you have one, it is much faster on a thick trunk: preferredTool): the part of the tree above it falls in the break direction and drops its logs plus 0-7 sticks (the part of a log left over). Every tree species uses the same rule (spruce and dark oak too): the stick count depends on how much wood falls, not on the species. Felling may give few or no sticks: for sticks, prefer dead bushes (deadbush-sticks) and leaves you can reach from the ground (leaves-sticks). Break the thinnest trunk you can reach (by hand about 1.5 s per hardness point: radius 4 about 6 s, radius 8 about 24 s) and stand to the side.
evidence: docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 1 step 4: [W-Getting_Started], [W-Tips] (trees fall in the chop direction; Dynamic Trees fork)

the dump: Dynamic Trees branch blocks dynamictrees:<wood>branch, material wood, toolRequired false (harvestTool axe, level 0); hardness = the log's hardness x radius^2 / 8 (oakbranch radius 1: 0.25, radius 2: 1), capped by config/dynamictrees.cfg line 114 maxTreeHardness=200 (BlockBranchBasic.func_176195_g)

mods/DramaticTrees-1.12.2-0.13.4.jar (SHA-256 b86dae768ccc1182c52e5b9a8756a5906da53dc125d48bfe1c8dc69204a77ffe; it holds the com.ferreusveritas.dynamictrees classes the dumped branches use): no tool check. BlockBranch.removedByPlayer -> removedByEntity -> FutureBreak -> futureBreak (bytecode 0-262): destroyBranchFromNode, getLogDrops(wood volume x (1 + 0.25 x Fortune level)), ForgeEventFactory.fireBlockHarvesting, EntityFallingTree.dropTree(HARVEST); the held item only adds Fortune and takes damageAxe

Logs and sticks: NodeNetVolume.run adds radius^2 x 64 voxels per branch block and getVolume divides by 4096; getLogDrops multiplies by config/dynamictrees.cfg line 108 harvestMultiplier=1.5; Species.getLogsAndSticks (bytecode 0-23): logs = floor(V), sticks = floor((V - logs) x 8), kept because line 96 dropSticks=true (Species$LogsAndSticks); DropCreatorLogs.getLogsDrop (bytecode 55-83) adds TreeFamily.getStick(n) = minecraft:stick (TreeFamily init bytecode 85-96, Items.field_151055_y)
No pack rule removes them: config/betterwithmods.cfg line 474 HCLumber=false, config/primallib.cfg line 37 No Tree Punching integration false, no scripts/dropt*.zs rule matches a branch

Dynamic Trees' own leaf drops have no stick: BlockDynamicLeaves.getDrops (bytecode 0-32) only calls Species.getLeavesDrops, whose drop creators are the seed (DropCreatorSeed.getLeavesDrop: 1 in 20, Fortune down to 1 in 10) and, on apple oaks, the apple; nothing calls TreeRegistry.registerDropCreator in DramaticTrees or the 6 Dynamic Trees addon jars; no scripts/dropt*.zs rule gives leaves a stick (only biomesoplenty:leaves_6:8/9, dropt_loose_materials.zs lines 701, 711). CORRECTION (2026-11-07, G3 round 8 A): this line used to say leaves give no sticks at all. That missed Pyrotech's own leaf handler, which adds a stick half the time when a player breaks leaves, Dynamic Trees leaves included: see the rule leaves-sticks

Species (lead's question after G3 round 8 A, spruce vs dark oak): in DramaticTrees no species class overrides Species.getLogsAndSticks, and the six vanilla families (oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak) share DropCreatorLogs and TreeFamily.getStick (minecraft:stick). Only some Biomes O' Plenty addon species (the twiglets, acacia brush, palm, bamboo, mangrove, hellbark) and the Aether addon's DropCreatorLogsAdvanced override it. NodeNetVolume.run adds radius x radius x 64 per branch block (an int), getVolume divides by 4096, and BlockBranch.getLogDrops multiplies by treeHarvestMultiplier (1.5), so V = 1.5 x the sum of radius^2 / 64 over the felled branches, in steps of 3/128. The stick count is the leftover eighths of V and changes with the tree's shape, not its species: the data cannot say that one species drops none (excerpts in packages/rotn-data/test/fixtures/stick-sources-3.3.4/stick-sources.javap.txt)

Supporting only (the bytecode above is the evidence): G3 smoke round 4 batch B (harness-ops captures/raw/r4-g3b/night/driver.log lines 162-164, 197-199, 214): every logged dynamictrees:leaves0 break gave no stick while the bot, with no axe, gained sticks; the log alone does not rule out other sources (crafting from planks, broken sticks, items already on the ground). The sticks it gained fit Pyrotech's leaf sticks (leaves-sticks), which land as items after the break

Supporting only: the yield is low in practice. G3 smoke round 5 A rerun (skills-rotn's note on the sticks step in src/agent/agenda.js): 3 felled spruces gave 25 logs and 1 stick. G3 round 8 A (harness-ops captures/raw/r8-g3a/rocks/driver.log lines 251 and 520): 2 felled spruces gave no stick, and the bot then held 32 logs (line 362), so logs from trees felled by hand do drop. 5 trees and 1 stick is far below the about 3.5 sticks per tree an even spread of the leftover would give. Not explained here: the shapes of these trees, or sticks that landed where the bot did not pick them up

sources.summary: Right-click the placed debarked log with the axe again: the block disappears and 1 plank drops one block toward you (1 axe use). This is how the first plank (for the crafting table) is made without a table: 1 log gives 1 plank for 2 axe uses, while a crafting table gives 3 planks per log. A few modded logs are the exception and craft into 4 planks in the 2x2 grid: the Biomes O' Plenty mangrove log, Pam's maple, cinnamon and paperbark logs, the Twilight Forest twilight oak log and the Stygian end log. Two Twilight Forest crafts also need no table: 4 dark twilight logs (2x2) give 4 tower wood, and a giant log gives 64 oak planks.

sources.summary: Break leaves by hand (or with any tool except shears): each leaf block drops 1 stick half the time (Pyrotech), on top of its usual drops. This works on Dynamic Trees leaves, which every vanilla tree here has, and on plain leaves. Leaves break fast by hand (hardness 0.2). Expect about 1 stick per 2 leaf blocks. Only break leaves you can reach from the ground; do not climb a tree for them.
evidence: mods/pyrotech-1.12.2-1.5.25.jar (SHA-256 2b28dd9274ca66e4d981547c4cce36bc081b2bc925d694dda4249f412cdbf36a): ModuleCore.onPreInitializationEvent (bytecode 87-106) registers HarvestDropsEventHandler$Sticks when ModuleCoreConfig$Tweaks.DROP_STICKS_FROM_LEAVES is true, and config/pyrotech/core.cfg line 8 sets B:DROP_STICKS_FROM_LEAVES=true. Its handler on(HarvestDropsEvent) takes the block's getItem stack (func_185473_a, the pick-block item); if athenaeum's OreDictHelper.contains("treeLeaves", stack) it adds 1 minecraft:stick (Items.field_151055_y) when Random.nextFloat() < 0.5 with a player harvester (bytecode 108-110, 147-172), or < 0.1 with none, e.g. decay (113-144). It only adds to the drops

Which leaves: the dump's ore treeLeaves holds minecraft:leaves and minecraft:leaves2 at every meta (32767). The vanilla leaves' getItem is the block's own item: BlockOldLeaf keeps Block's default (Item.getItemFromBlock(this), damageDropped), and BlockNewLeaf returns minecraft:leaves2 at meta & 3 (Forge-patched classes). Dynamic Trees leaves: BlockDynamicLeaves.func_185473_a returns getProperties(state).getPrimitiveLeavesItemStack(), built in LeavesPropertiesJson.getPrimitiveLeaves (bytecode 28-67) as Item.getItemFromBlock(block) at damageDropped from the 'leaves' state named in DramaticTrees' assets/dynamictrees/leaves/common.json: minecraft:leaves variant oak, spruce, birch, jungle and minecraft:leaves2 variant acacia, dark_oak

The event fires with the player for these leaves: Forge's BlockLeaves overrides neither harvestBlock nor the drop path (its dropBlockAsItemWithChance only calls Block's), BlockDynamicLeaves overrides none of harvestBlock, dropBlockAsItemWithChance, dropBlockAsItem or removedByPlayer, and Block.dropBlockAsItemWithChance (Forge-patched) calls getDrops, then ForgeEventFactory.fireBlockHarvesting with harvesters.get(), the player that Block.harvestBlock set
Shears: Forge's BlockLeaves is IShearable, so shears take the leaf block itself through onSheared, not the harvest drops
Excerpts of every class above, with the jar SHA-256s and Forge's binpatch and SRG steps: packages/rotn-data/test/fixtures/stick-sources-3.3.4/stick-sources.javap.txt

sources.summary: Break a dead bush (minecraft:deadbush) by hand or with any tool except shears: it breaks at once (hardness 0) and drops 0, 1 or 2 sticks, 1 on average, so plan on about 3 bushes for 3 sticks. Shears give the dead bush itself and no sticks. Dead bushes stand on sand, red sand, terracotta or dirt.
evidence: minecraft_server.1.12.2.jar (SHA-256 fe1f9274e6dad9191bf6e6e8e36ee6ebc737f373603df0946aafcded0d53167e) with Forge 14.23.5.2860's server binpatch for net.minecraft.block.BlockDeadBush (apu) applied (binpatches.pack.lzma in forge-1.12.2-14.23.5.2860.jar, SHA-256 cd3fbf85d7ca744507fd6a37a41b90122d43e616a4f8962332b1b658655e8a64; the patch's input checksum matches the shipped class), names from the Forge jar's SRG table: getItemDropped (func_180660_a) returns Items.STICK (air.B = field_151055_y) for any state and Fortune, and quantityDropped (func_149745_a) returns Random.nextInt(3): 0, 1 or 2 sticks, 1 on average. The binpatch leaves both as in vanilla and only adds IShearable

Shears: harvestBlock (func_180657_a) drops one dead bush instead when the held item is Items.SHEARS (field_151097_aZ, bytecode 0-43), and the Forge patch adds isShearable true and onSheared -> 1 dead bush

Where it stands: canSustainBush (func_185514_i, x) accepts sand (Blocks.field_150354_m, red sand is its meta 1), hardened clay (field_150405_ch), stained hardened clay (field_150406_ce) and dirt (field_150346_d). mods/BBLSOhMy-1.1.2.jar (SHA-256 b549e8280663f7e233fb9b930ddc36b7c9a2415c0900e644a254d769fa41f20e) BlockDeadBushMixin only widens that check (@ModifyReturnValue on canSustainBush, mixins.bblsom.refmap.json) to its own fertile blocks; it does not touch the drops

No pack rule changes the drop: no scripts/**/*.zs line names the dead bush, and every one of the 248 Dropt rules in scripts/ has a block matcher, none naming it (Pyrotech's own Dropt rules are off: config/pyrotech/plugin.Dropt.cfg). In config/ it appears only in settings that do not touch its drop: config/inspirations.cfg line 489 (bonemeal on sand grows a dead bush), cyclicmagic.cfg line 54 (the magic bean's drop list), arcanearchives.cfg line 113, AdPother's fuel list, tool_progression/blocks.cfg lines 41697-41698 (no harvest level)

Mod jars: every class in mods/*.jar that names Blocks.field_150330_I, net/minecraft/block/BlockDeadBush or 'deadbush' was checked, and none changes its drop: Inspirations TweaksEvents.bonemealPlants places one; Better With Addons InteractionBWR.init adds a cauldron recipe (sapling -> dead bush); EndReborn ToolEntropyWand.convert7 turns a block into one; the rest are world generation, loot tables, recipes, fuel and flower pots. Of the 64 HarvestDropsEvent handler classes in mods/, the 5 that name a plant type (BlockBush, IPlantable, IShearable) do not apply: Better With Mods MushroomFarming (BlockMushroom only), DungeonTactics DTEventHandler (ore clusters), Hunger Overhaul's onBlockHarvested (exact crop classes; it returns at bytecode 264-269 for any other block), ToroQuest EventHandlers.harvestDrops (counts drops for a mining quest, changes none), Inspirations TweaksEvents (beetroot, carrots and potatoes). The other 59 name neither the dead bush nor a plant type and were not each read

the dump: minecraft:deadbush has one state (meta 0, net.minecraft.block.BlockDeadBush), hardness 0, no tool, no collision box. Its fixed-seed drop sample is empty (nextInt(3) gave 0 for that seed), which is why the dump's plain drops miss it

sources.summary: Break dirt, grass, podzol, coarse dirt, mycelium, a grass path or dry farmland by hand, or with any tool except a shovel of mining level 1 or higher: it drops 4 Piles of Dirt (betterwithmods:dirt_pile), not a dirt block. 4 piles make 1 dirt in the 2x2 grid (shapeless, no table). A flint, bone, quartz, redstone or iron shovel (level 1 or higher) gets the dirt block instead; the crude, wooden, stone and golden shovels are level 0 and still give piles.
evidence: scripts/dropt_loose_materials.zs lines 4-16 (cited lines in packages/rotn-data/test/fixtures/rotn-3.3.4/dirt-drops.excerpt.txt): Dropt list "pile_dirt" matches growthcraft_rice:ricepaddy, minecraft:dirt, minecraft:grass, minecraft:mycelium, minecraft:dirt:1, minecraft:dirt:2, minecraft:farmland, minecraft:grass_path, betterwithmods:fertile_farmland and pyrotech:farmland_mulched for a PLAYER harvester whose main hand is not on the blacklist "shovel;1;-1", and drops <betterwithmods:dirt_pile> with Dropt.range(4)

mods/dropt-1.12.2-1.19.4.jar (SHA-256 21837ce855ad3304fa2aa2cc4d29fe5989cd61f09fa8fc1f9f4e53dedbacfd04; excerpts in packages/rotn-data/test/fixtures/dropt-1.19.4/Dropt.javap.txt): HeldItemMatcher.matches (bytecode 169-256) fails a BLACKLIST rule only when the held item's tool classes contain the tool class and its harvest level is within [min, max]; ParserRuleMatchHarvesterHeldItem (441-577) splits "shovel;1;-1" at ";" and turns a max below 0 into 2147483647, so the excluded items are shovels of level 1 or higher; DroptAPI.range(int) sets a fixed count (4). A rule replaces the drops (Rule.replaceStrategy defaults to REPLACE_ALL). athenaeum-1.12.2-1.19.6.jar RecipeItemParser.parse sets meta 0 before reading the string, so a block named without a meta (minecraft:dirt, minecraft:farmland) matches meta 0 only: wet farmland (metas 1-7) keeps its plain drop

config/betterwithmods.cfg line 495: HCPiles=false (Better With Mods' own pile drops are off), and config/pyrotech/plugin.Dropt.cfg lines 22 and 26: Pyrotech's dirt and grass Dropt rules are off; scripts/dropt.zs names no dirt or grass block. So the pile_dirt rule is the only drop change for these blocks

the dump: crafttweaker:ct_shapeless281424108 is shapeless, 4 betterwithmods:dirt_pile -> 1 minecraft:dirt, requiresTable false (scripts/minecraft_(max-file-size).zs lines 218 and 268); the item betterwithmods:dirt_pile is "Pile of Dirt" (item.bwm:dirt_pile), stack size 256

Supporting only: the human, who plays the pack, via the lead (2026-11-06): breaking dirt by hand works but drops dirt pieces, not a dirt block, and 4 pieces in a 2x2 grid craft one dirt block. G3 smoke round 6 (the lead, #284): the bot ended up with Better With Mods dirt piles instead of dirt
unverified: no harness run has checked the count of 4 (the round 6 bot's inventory was not counted)
sources.note: The same script turns other soils into their own piles the same way (lines 17-110): Biomes O' Plenty silty, loamy and sandy dirt into contenttweaker:silty_dirt_pile, loamy_dirt_pile and sandy_dirt_pile; Defiled Lands dirt and grass into contenttweaker:defiled_dirt_pile; Aether dirt and grass into contenttweaker:aether_dirt_pile; Better With Mods dirt slabs into 2 dirt piles; contenttweaker:rocky_dirt into 2 dirt piles and a rock. Sand, red sand and gravel drop 4 sand, red sand and gravel piles (lines 113-152). Not encoded here.

sources.summary: Dig dirt or grass with a shovel of mining level 1 or higher (flint, bone, quartz, redstone or iron): the pack's pile rule does not apply, so the block drops itself as dirt (coarse dirt gives coarse dirt; grass, podzol, mycelium, a grass path and farmland give dirt).
evidence: the dump (blocks.json drops, getItemDropped): minecraft:dirt metas 0 and 2, minecraft:grass, minecraft:mycelium, minecraft:farmland, minecraft:grass_path, betterwithmods:fertile_farmland and pyrotech:farmland_mulched drop minecraft:dirt; minecraft:dirt meta 1 (coarse) drops minecraft:dirt:1

the pile_dirt rule excludes these shovels (see dirt-piles): mods/dropt-1.12.2-1.19.4.jar (SHA-256 21837ce855ad3304fa2aa2cc4d29fe5989cd61f09fa8fc1f9f4e53dedbacfd04; excerpts in packages/rotn-data/test/fixtures/dropt-1.19.4/Dropt.javap.txt): HeldItemMatcher.matches (bytecode 169-256) fails a BLACKLIST rule only when the held item's tool classes contain the tool class and its harvest level is within [min, max]; ParserRuleMatchHarvesterHeldItem (441-577) splits "shovel;1;-1" at ";" and turns a max below 0 into 2147483647, so the excluded items are shovels of level 1 or higher; DroptAPI.range(int) sets a fixed count (4). A rule replaces the drops (Rule.replaceStrategy defaults to REPLACE_ALL). athenaeum-1.12.2-1.19.6.jar RecipeItemParser.parse sets meta 0 before reading the string, so a block named without a meta (minecraft:dirt, minecraft:farmland) matches meta 0 only: wet farmland (metas 1-7) keeps its plain drop

the dump (items.json toolClasses): shovel level 1 or higher: pyrotech:flint_shovel, bone_shovel, quartz_shovel and redstone_shovel, minecraft:iron_shovel and iceandfire:silver_shovel (1), minecraft:diamond_shovel and pyrotech:obsidian_shovel (2); level 0: pyrotech:crude_shovel, minecraft:wooden_shovel, stone_shovel and golden_shovel
unverified: no harness run has dug dirt with a level 1 shovel yet
